key_insight: Introduce a meta-cognitive decision layer that lets agentic multimodal models judge whether to answer from internal perception or call external tools, substantially reducing reflexive (and often unnecessary) tool invocation and its associated costs.
problem_solved: Agentic multimodal systems habitually overuse external utilities—invoking tools reflexively even when the visual context suffices—causing extra latency, cost, and brittle behaviors; the paper tackles the arbitration between internal reasoning and tool use.
method: Add a meta-cognitive controller that estimates internal-confidence and compares expected internal utility vs. external-tool cost to gate tool calls.
Train/finetune agents with cost-aware objectives and self-reflection signals (e.g., calibrated confidence, contrastive examples) so they learn when to rely on perception vs. tools.
Evaluate with multimodal tasks and metrics that measure unnecessary tool calls, latency, and task accuracy to verify more efficient, reliable behavior.
impact: Makes agentic multimodal systems faster, cheaper, and more robust by preventing unnecessary tool use—important for real-world deployment and scalable multi-tool agent architectures.
visual_elements: Flowchart showing decision gate: Visual input → internal reasoning (confidence) → gate → tool invocation or direct answer.

Interaction timeline (sequence diagram) demonstrating an example query resolved internally vs. one that requires a tool.
paper_title: Act Wisely: Cultivating Meta-Cognitive Tool Use in Agentic Multimodal Models
paper_authors: Shilin Yan, Jintao Tong, Hongwei Xue, Xiaojun Tang, Yangyang Wang
